correctness.rationale: For any positive b and n, the exact identity 4n·binom((b+4)n,4n)=(bn+1)·binom((b+4)n,4n-1) proves odd-prime divisibility and reduces odd b,odd n to ≤1 binary carry in an addition. At all odd depths h≥3, the explicit seven-coordinate binary-state transition has 4 reachable states at depth 3, 11 at depth 5, and the depth-5 set is invariant under two transitions. Each reachable terminal state with 3n−1<2^h has a capped count of at least two carries, proving every smaller index works. At the explicit index (2^h+1)/3 the carry count is ν₂((b+3)/2^h)≤1, so it fails. checker.py reconstructs and checks the finite state sets and tests 6689 assertions, while the all-b conclusion follows from the invariant rather than finite samples.

value.rationale: The first-failure function is a directly motivated natural invariant from Sun’s explicit binomial divisibility problem. The theorem completely evaluates a whole fixed-parameter family for every positive b, obtains unbounded thresholds 1,3,11,43,… with exact odd/even 2-adic plateaus, and gives an all-depth structural carry obstruction. This is more than a known existence bound, a routine single-instance Kummer computation, or an arbitrary finite slice.
